ig_carousel_topic.topic: Bankroll math for people who've never thought about bankroll
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Most bettors lose money before they ever make a bad pick.
The math is the problem, not the picks.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common approach: bet whatever feels right per game.
Some nights $50, some nights $200 when you're confident.
That variance alone will wipe you out during a normal cold streak.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Flat betting a fixed unit size is the baseline that actually works.
One unit equals 1 to 2 percent of your total bankroll.
That cap keeps a 5-game losing streak from ending your season.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example: $1,000 bankroll. One unit = $15 (1.5%).
A 5-game losing streak costs $75. You're still in the game.
Bet $100 a game? Same streak costs $500. Now you're chasing.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
A 54% win rate at flat 1.5% units produces real, compounding returns over a full season.
The edge is meaningless if a bad week zeros the account first.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Bankroll math is where most bettors quietly lose before a single bad pick. One unit. 1 to 2 percent. It compounds.
